issues.legal_issue: A person who manages property or collects its rents cannot grant a substantial interest in it without authority to dispose of the property.
material_facts: A purported agent granted a raiyati settlement over the disputed land to the appellant.
There was no written authority for the grant, and the evidence did not establish that the purported agent had authority to dispose of the property.
The evidence of management and rent collection, and references to the purported agent as a local agent, did not establish authority to transfer or dispose of the land.
issues.conclusion: The purported agent lacked proven authority to grant the settlement, so it did not bind the owner; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that a person may transfer property not their own only if authorised to dispose of it. Authority to manage property or collect rents does not, without evidence of authority to dispose of the property, establish authority to grant a substantial interest in it. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.property_settlement_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a purported settlement of property binds its owner.
predicates.settlement_granted_by_agent: A person purporting to act for the owner granted an interest in the property.
predicates.no_evidence_of_authority_to_dispose: The evidence did not show that the purported agent was authorised to dispose of the property.

issues.definition: When a property settlement dispute concerns an interest granted by an agent and there is no evidence that the agent was authorised to dispose of the property, the settlement is not binding on the owner.

issues.legal_issue: A property owner is not estopped from denying a claimant’s title merely because rent receipts indicate payment to the owner when the owner’s knowledge and consent are not proved.
material_facts: Rent receipts indicated that the appellant had paid rents to the owner.
There was no evidence that the rents were collected with the owner’s knowledge and consent, and the receipts were not put to the owner or her husband at trial.
The owner’s case was that rent collectors had collected the rents without accounting to her or handing them over.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not establish estoppel against the owner.
issues.legal_principle: The court rejected estoppel because there was no evidence that rent was collected from the claimant with the owner’s knowledge and consent. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.estoppel_defense_in_property_dispute: A claimant in a property dispute argues that the owner is estopped from denying the claimant’s title.
predicates.rent_receipts_indicate_payment_to_owner: Receipts indicate that the claimant paid rent to the owner.
predicates.owner_knowledge_and_consent_not_proved: The evidence does not establish that the owner knew of and consented to the rent collection.

issues.definition: When a claimant relies on rent receipts in a property dispute but the owner’s knowledge and consent to the rent collection are not proved, estoppel is not established.
